result.title: Annotrace: A Workbench for Step-Level Annotation of Agent Traces
result.comment: 4 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Under review at the AAAI 2027 Demonstration Program
result.summary: Every study of why LLM agents fail begins by labelling traces by hand, and every such study builds its own throwaway tool. Observability platforms record agent traces but offer no structured labelling; annotation tools label text but have no notion of a step, a delegation or a tool call, leaving it unclear what the smallest unit of execution to label should be. Annotrace reads six trace formats, including OpenTelemetry GenAI, LangSmith and Langfuse, and turns each run into an ordered, nested list of steps. The annotator writes their own labelling codebook; a frontier model proposes a starting set from a sample of their own traces, answers first, and is asked exactly the questions the human is asked, making annotation a joint human-AI process. Annotrace measures agreement between any two annotators, human or AI. On a multi-agent question-answering corpus it reproduces a previous manual effort's 235 annotation units exactly, and two models labelling the same traces agree 91% of the time at $κ= 0.82$.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Annotrace：读取六种 trace 格式（含 OpenTelemetry GenAI、LangSmith、Langfuse），把每次运行转成有序嵌套的 step 列表，支持人类自写 codebook、前沿模型先答同一套问题，并度量人-AI 或 AI-AI 标注一致性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「最小可标注执行单元」的切分方式与标注一致性（κ）度量，可能为 LVR 中 latent 推理步的划分、逐步监督与轨迹标注评价提供可核查的现成线索；但面向文本 agent trace，迁移到多模态推理状态仍需验证。
